en: Jose Rizal wrote the novel Noli Me Tangere to expose the abuses of the Spanish friars in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, or Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and is endemic to the forests of Mindanao.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of the Cordilleras over two thousand years ago.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white jasmine flower, was officially declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian to study at Harvard Medical School and invented a bamboo incubator.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, located in Manila, is the highest court and holds the judicial branch.
During the Sinulog Festival in Cebu, devotees dance to honor the Santo Niño, the Holy Child Jesus.
Filipino and English are the two official languages of the Philippines, alongside over a hundred regional languages like Cebuano.
The South Sea pearl, harvested from the Pinctada maxima oyster, is the official national gem of the Philippines.
Every Filipino citizen has the constitutional right to vote in national elections once they reach the age of eighteen.
Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the Bonifacio Monument in Caloocan and the Oblation statue at the University of the Philippines.
